title: Feature Expansion for Graph Neural Networks
summary: The paper tackles node classification with GNNs by analyzing the feature space that drives representation learning, which the authors argue has never been systematically studied: they decompose linear approximations of spatial and spectral GNNs into fixed feature subspaces (functions of node attributes and graph structure matrices) and trainable reweighting parameters. They prove that sequentially aggregated feature subspaces tend to become linearly correlated (Prop. 3.1), so the common weight-sharing mechanism bounds expressiveness (Thm. 3.2) and low-dimensional node attributes limit the space further; they therefore propose FE-GNN, a purely linear model that flattens subspaces with independent per-subspace weights and appends structural principal components from a truncated SVD of the adjacency matrix (Eq. 11). On random 60%/20%/20% splits averaged over 100 runs, FE-GNN matches or beats SoTA on five homophilic graphs and improves accuracy by 32.0% on average over GCN on three heterophilic graphs - e.g., 73.33% on Chameleon vs 64.06% for the best baseline - with comparable per-epoch training time.

match_target.why: User-hinted target, and the paper's headline heterophilic result: Chameleon (128-dim attributes, h(G)=0.23) is exactly the case the authors say modification 2 addresses, and the margin over every baseline is largest here (73.33 vs 64.06 for the best baseline, vs 61.85 for GCN). It is also the cheapest claim that still shows the central result - it needs only the FE-GNN (C) model on a 2,277-node graph (~62 ms SVD + ~2.8 s per run, ~5 min for the full 100-run protocol on one GPU), whereas C8 additionally requires training the GCN baseline and C2-C4/C7 use larger graphs.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: bounded accuracy-like score on a test set smaller than 2,000 examples - Chameleon has 2,277 nodes, so the 20% test split is only ~455 nodes, failing rule 2's 2,000-example threshold; and the ±0.35 the paper prints is a 95% confidence interval over 100 runs, not a std, so rule 1 does not apply. Band = 2.0 absolute points.

requirements.stmt: Implement the FE-GNN output as a sum of independently reweighted feature subspaces plus a structural-component subspace: H = sum_{k=0}^{K} P_k(L) X W^(k) + S W_s, with a separate, non-shared weight matrix W^(k) for every polynomial order k (feature subspace flattening).
requirements.quote: FE-GNN uses independent parameter matrices W (k) and Ws to reweight each feature subspace to provide flexible reweighting

requirements.stmt: Construct S as the structural principal components: a truncated SVD of the graph structure matrix, keeping |S| top singular vectors scaled by their singular values; for Chameleon |S| = 700.
requirements.quote: we propose to construct the expansion subspace using the truncated SVD of the structural matrix, called structural principal components as modification 2

requirements.stmt: Keep the model purely linear: no activation functions, no dropout, no DropEdge or other deep artifices; the only nonlinearity is the softmax inside the cross-entropy loss.
requirements.quote: our implementation is purely linear without any deep artifices such as activation functions or dropout except for the cross-entropy loss

requirements.stmt: Apply column-wise L2 normalization to the feature subspaces (each column of the concatenated feature matrix normalized to unit norm) before reweighting, so all columns contribute equally.
requirements.quote: we add a column-wise normalization to ensure that each column of each feature subspace contributes equally to the whole feature space

requirements.stmt: Evaluate with random 60%/20%/20% train/validation/test splits (not the public Planetoid/Geom-GCN splits) and report the mean result over 100 runs.
requirements.quote: We test on the node classification task with random 60%/20%/20% splits and summarize the results of 100 runs

requirements.stmt: Report classification accuracy (micro F1) with a 95% confidence interval across the runs.
requirements.quote: We report the average accuracy (micro F1 score) in the classification task with a 95% confidence interval

requirements.stmt: Optimize with Adam and use early stopping with a warmup of 50 epochs and a patience of 200 epochs.
requirements.quote: We employ Adam for optimization and set the early stopping criteria as a warmup of 50 pluses patience of 200

requirements.stmt: Use the Table 8 Chameleon configuration: learning rate 0.01, weight decay 0.0005, |S| = 700, hidden size 64, polynomial order k = 3 (selected from the grid-search spaces listed in App. B.2).
For the FE-GNN (C) variant targeted here, build the polynomial feature subspaces with the Chebyshev basis (the monomial basis defines the separate FE-GNN (M) variant).
requirements.quote: FE-GNN uses the Chebyshev or monomial polynomials to construct the feature space, and we refer to the corresponding versions as FE-GNN (C) and FE-GNN (M)

requirements.stmt: Use the renormalized adjacency matrix A_hat = (D+I)^(-1/2)(A+I)(D+I)^(-1/2) and the corresponding normalized Laplacian L_hat = I - A_hat everywhere (both in the polynomial terms and as input to the SVD).
requirements.quote: using the eigendecomposition of the Laplacian matrix: ˆL = I −ˆA = UΛU T

requirements.stmt: Train with the cross-entropy loss between node labels and the softmax of the linear model output.
requirements.quote: to minimize the difference between node label Y and the obtained representation

requirements.stmt: Load all datasets through PyTorch Geometric and treat every graph as undirected.
requirements.quote: We set these datasets to undirected graphs as we assumed in the Preliminaries.
